item.description:
### Changed - **Help:** articles now say exactly what the app does: the wizards go by name (an object made in the portal under one of their names is treated as theirs); Private Access re-runs can update the wizard's segments and rules; Undo doesn't retry a setting or rule changed since; and when Client Connector removes a new forwarding profile after a failed app profile. Help also covers AI Guard in POV Start, the change log and the API client's access, and lists where each Undo and Check for Drift is. - **Bulk Rule Manager:** the delete confirmations now say exactly what's checked. For ZIA, each rule or custom object is read again just before it's deleted, and left in place if that read shows a different name. For Private Access, the objects are read again before the first delete, and nothing is deleted if that read would change the preview. A change made in the portal after that read isn't caught, except that a segment isn't taken out of, or put back into, a segment group renamed since the preview.
### Fixed - **POV Start, Tenant Readiness:** a Private Access role that's listed without its permissions is no longer passed because its name says full access or super admin; each permission the wizard needs is shown as not checked. If Private Access answers the role list with something that isn't a list, the row now says it couldn't read the permissions, rather than treating the role as missing from the list. - **Client Connector:** when Client Connector refuses an app profile change that carried a password (one typed in Edit Existing Profiles, or the wizard's tamper protection password), the error now shows the HTTP status without Client Connector's answer, since the answer could repeat the password. For the wizard, the summary report leaves the answer out too. Without a password, the answer is shown as before. - **Client Connector:** when a profile create gets no answer, a profile of that name is kept on the run's record only when it holds the tamper protection password this run sent (and its settings), so Undo doesn't remove another admin's profile made from the same template at the same time. A forwarding profile found that way is no longer put on the record: Apply says to check the Mobile Admin portal, and running the wizard again with the same ZPW- name updates or keeps that profile. Two runs that use the same typed password still can't be told apart. An answer that's empty, unreadable or doesn't say the create succeeded is now treated the same as no answer, rather than as a success. - **Private Access, Manage:** when a delete fails after a segment was taken out of its segment group, putting it back now checks that the group still has the name the preview showed and that Private Access answered with the whole group; otherwise nothing is sent and the result says to add the segment back in the portal, so an incomplete answer can no longer take the group's other segments out of it. The result names the group (it showed "?" before). Taking a segment out of its group now makes the same check that Private Access answered with the whole group; if it didn't, nothing is sent and the delete still goes ahead, as after any take-out that fails. - **AI Guard, Apply:** when ZIA or AI Guard doesn't answer a create, Apply no longer takes an object of that name as its own, since it could be another admin's, so Undo can't remove someone else's object. A create answered without an ID is handled the same way. The step says to check the tenant, the steps that need the object are skipped, and after such a ZIA create ZIA is now activated, in case it went through. When ZIA doesn't allow the SSL Inspection rule above its predefined rules and doesn't confirm it below them either, the warning now says it may be there, rather than that it is. Running the dry run again finds the object by name and finishes the rest. If this run did make it, it isn't on the run's record: delete it in the portal if you don't want it. - **AI Guard:** when ZIA answers a read with something other than the list or settings asked for, Undo now stops and keeps the change for next time instead of counting it as already gone or changed since, and no longer removes a proxy or certificate when the list of what might use it couldn't be read. That includes a list with an entry that doesn't clearly show which proxy or certificate it uses: the proxy or certificate stays for a later Undo, and Undo carries on with the rest. Undo also stops on a list entry with no ID, and on settings missing a prompt switch the run turned on. The dry run shows such a read as a problem instead of planning on an empty list (a list of proxies or proxy gateways with an entry like that too), and Apply's prompt capture step fails without changing anything. When the settings can't be read there, that step no longer says the change may have been made. A picked app's prompt switch that ZIA shows as neither on nor off now stops the dry run, and one to turn on that Apply's last read doesn't show as on or off stops that step, so Undo never turns off a switch whose earlier value it couldn't know. - **ZIA changes wait for a running change:** while a change to the tenant runs (an Apply, Undo or Manage change in any product, a Bulk Rule Manager deletion, an SSL certificate change, an AI Guard or Policy Simulator change, POV Start's Apply All), the buttons for a ZIA Policy Apply or Undo, an SSL certificate change or its Undo, a Bulk Rule Manager deletion, POV Start's Apply All and a Policy Simulator change to the tenant or its Undo now wait for it, as AI Guard's Apply and Undo already did, and all of them, AI Guard's too, now say what they're waiting for. ZIA's activation makes every pending change live, so one change's activation could make another's half-done changes live. New POV and Resume are refused until it finishes, so starting a new POV no longer clears a running AI Guard Apply or Undo. A stopped Apply, or one whose activation failed, still isn't activated, but what it saved stays pending and goes live at the next activation from anywhere, including the ZIA portal: the Apply page and Help now say so, so undo it first if it shouldn't go live. - **POV Start, Apply All:** applies only the dry runs you reviewed and confirmed. A product whose dry run is run again or stopped, or whose choices change, after you confirm is now left out and named on the page instead of applied, and one that had nothing to change when you confirmed isn't applied by that run. Running any product's dry run again, here or on its own page, now unticks "I've reviewed each dry run", and it shows unticked while the products in scope differ from the ones you ticked it for. - **POV Start, New POV:** a new POV, from the defaults or a template, now takes the tenant's Cloud Sandbox licence and Cloud Firewall edition again, instead of keeping the ones picked on Customize, loaded from a file or resumed in the last POV. When the tenant's subscriptions don't say which, it takes the template's or the defaults' (Advanced Sandbox, no Cloud Firewall edition, which keeps every firewall rule). Resuming a POV saved without a Cloud Firewall edition now takes the tenant's edition too, instead of the last POV's. - **Active POVs:** a change on ZIA › AI Guard is now saved with the open POV as you make it, like the other wizards'. Before, it was saved only with your next change elsewhere, a page change, or when the POV closed. - **Active POVs, Continue:** on the POV already open, Continue now keeps what's in the wizards and saves it, then goes where you left off. Before, it put back the POV's last save: a change made in the last moment or two was lost, every wizard's Apply results were cleared, and Client Connector got a new tamper protection password. Looking at the Active POVs list no longer makes it the place Resume returns to, or counts as activity on the POV. - **POV Start, Fill the Modules:** with no customer name, no POV is saved; the intake now says to name the customer, and Active POVs says why nothing was saved.
